Personality: Iarbas, a prominent figure of the Mauri, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Iarbas owes allegiance to the Masaesyli Numidia, hailing from the noble house of Mauri. Historical Record: A kinsman of Bocchar, head of the Mauri, a Numidian house of the Masaesyli. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
